decisions.reason: “Battlefield” fits the scene; SOL preserves the sense that everyone thought the Blood Lord was dead.

SOL conveys both disbelief and the unavoidable reality; the following hunk continues the action.

“Pale” preserves the source; “deathly” adds emphasis.
The red-stained surroundings are retained in the next hunk.
SOL restores the red-stained image and preserves the blood obscuring the Force.

“Sacred martyrdom” keeps the meaning without the unnecessary article.
“This had gone beyond madness” preserves the escalation.
“His survival” makes the calamity’s referent clear from context.

“Grow over its charred body” naturally preserves the regeneration.

SOL preserves the lips’ being fused and the teeth revealed.
SOL keeps the tongue’s color, movement, and thirst-driven cause.

SOL preserves the fleeting thought of retreat to delay recovery.

The rhetorical question about the clearer voice remains intact.
“Majestic” better preserves the grandeur of 웅혼한 공력 than “powerful.”
“Silent scream” naturally conveys the scream in his heart.
The source emphasizes the Force’s more intense light; SOL preserves that without adding power.
The source says the fanatics were scattered as well as cut to pieces; SOL drops the scattering.
The source’s 돌파 is a breakthrough; BASE preserves the established rendering.
“Behind him” clearly refers to Cheongpung and keeps the guards’ charge.
SOL preserves the troops’ range from Supreme First Rate to Peak in natural English.
SOL keeps their discarded armor, pride, vows, and shared direction.
“Toward the Blood Lord” naturally continues the preceding direction.
The source includes a deafening roar; “deafening crash” retains that sound more clearly than “impact.”
“A narrow gap began to open” naturally conveys the first breach in the ranks.
The source frames pill-taking as a concession; “Even with” preserves that contrast.
The source emphasizes getting closer both by a step and by even a moment; SOL drops the time element.
“At this rate” preserves the hopeful thought.
The source explicitly says they had to accomplish it; BASE retains the object of the resolve.
The next hunk states that Cheongpung was not alone in thinking so.

“Wrap his arms around” preserves the Daoist’s act of embracing the fanatic.
“Holding in” naturally conveys forcibly containing the spilling entrails.
SOL preserves the instinctive knowledge in concise, natural English.
“Given them the chance” naturally preserves Jin Taekyung’s creation of the opportunity.
“Slaughtered” preserves the source’s total destruction of the defenders and civilians.

The Korean says allies; “defenders” narrows the group without support.
SOL preserves the final charge and the certainty that none would regret it.
The bodies crumple and collapse; “fell” loses that physical image.
“But it was enough” keeps the meaning and flows naturally.
The sentence break and “Right now” preserve the contrast and immediate focus.
Cheongpung is the viewpoint character; SOL makes the unknown object clear without changing the beat.
“Its neck gone” preserves the decapitated corpse image in natural English.
The next hunk retains the dozens of bodies at the monster’s feet.
SOL combines the bodies and mummy-like corpses without dropping either detail.
“Looked and sounded genuinely curious” preserves the expression and tone.

SOL preserves the hand’s speed and the purple light from Cheongpung’s fingertips.
“With the pain” preserves the memories rising alongside it.
“As though in a trance” naturally preserves the entranced gesture.

The Korean describes their bodies crossing; SOL shifts the movement to Cheongpung alone.

SOL preserves the returning thirst as blood loss increases.
The storm of sword strikes and the Blood Lord looking around with growing thirst remain intact.
SOL preserves Cheongpung’s last strength and the lack of time to drink.
“Crack” and “Crunch” suit the two forceful impact sounds in context.
SOL combines the insufficient blood and its limited effect on his wounds.

“Delight” preserves his joy naturally.
SOL preserves the eager cry without the redundant “in an eager voice.”
The source says his arm stopped for an instant; SOL makes the Blood Lord himself stop.
The context and following sentence establish that both arms were cut; “them” is clear.
SOL preserves both arms flying up and the simultaneous pain and thirst.
“Kept smiling” naturally preserves that his smile did not fade.
The next hunk states what he knew, so the standalone lead-in is unnecessary.
SOL keeps the shadows, blocked rain, and sky turning black; the next hunk states the thirst payoff.
The explicit payoff is supported by the source and the following description.
The sound rings out from the air; “from above” changes its stated source.
“He saw them” clearly leads into the flying beasts.
The source emphatically corrects itself and says everyone saw clearly; SOL drops both emphases.
The source stresses that the beasts are too numerous to count; SOL omits that quantity.
SOL preserves the being at the center and far end of the approaching creatures.
“No one could block or evade” preserves the wave’s unstoppable, unavoidable force.
The source’s voice pierces Cheongpung’s ears as the wings cover the space; SOL weakens both images.

SOL preserves the tearing flesh and bone and the blood obscuring Cheongpung’s vision.
